subject: reactive expression didn't update when reactive source changed(item in list)

messages.author: 26b647b408a2e02e
messages.subject: reactive expression didn't update when reactive source changed(item in list)
parts:
I have some reactive values saved as multiple level of list. 

values$data
                   $merged
                                 $data: a data.table
                                 $info: another data.table

Now I have a reactive expression "select_data" that select a subset of "values$data", including a subset of "values$data$merged$data". 

Another reactive expression will update "values$data$merged$data", and I want "select_data" to update because the upstream data changed.

calc <- reactive({
  # update values$data$merged$data
  return(select_data())
})

However "select_data" didn't update. Could it because there are many levels in the list? However "select_data" did access the item "values$data$merged$data" directly.

Another possibility is that "values$data$merged$data" is a data.table. The modification of data.table is by reference, maybe this didn't trigger the change in reactive context. I tried to use "data.table::copy" but that didn't have any effect in trigger changes.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: reactive expression didn't update when reactive source changed(item in list)
parts:
It's true that modifying a data.table won't trigger reactivity. We don't have any way to know the data table object has changed.

Also, modifying a reactive values object is an example of a side effect and therefore should be done in an observer, not a reactive expression. If you don't know what I'm talking about, the "Effective reactive programming" videos on https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/ go into side effects and observers/reactives in some detail.

messages.subject: Re: reactive expression didn't update when reactive source changed(item in list)
parts:
Yes, actually my original plan of reactive expression is like that, but I ends up modifying reactive values because of another reactive expression, let me see if I can explain the situation as simple as possible.
There are pages for different features in my app:
   page A: some plots. The data is location and time of animal movements. There could be multiple animals in one data set.
   User can select a subset of animals in dataset, and that subset will be the data source for all the plots and features. If no row in a DT is selected, "current page" of the DT is selected. otherwise selected rows of the DT are selected. 
   This selection is done by reactive expression "select_data()".
   Page C need to calculate some additional columns which is only used in page C. It also need to use "select_data()" to obtain the subset.

1. I can just obtain the subset then calculate the columns, very simple. But I want to calculate the columns for all animals once then various subset will not need to calculate again. So I decided to change the whole data instead of the subset.

2. If I modify the whole data, I need to use the "select_data()" reactive to select the subset, which I thought it should work because its data source (whole data) has changed.

After fixing the data.table trigger problem, this worked, but there is another problem. Now if user move to page C then move to page A, the underlying data changed so page A plots refreshes, which could take some time, but the data used for plot didn't change.

This just as you said, not an optimal solution. I should keep the extra column separate from page A.

Another solution is copy the whole data, hold in an reactive, use another "select_data" procedure to select the subset again. I just need to abstract the selection process to function, and create two "select_data" reactive, one is solely used for page C. 

I wanted to reuse the "select_data" because it's not very simple, turned out this created more problem.

Now when I look back, method 1 of get subset and calculate may not that bad. It will not cause page A refresh, and it's very simple to implement. There could be some extra calculations but that may be faster than plot refreshes. Maybe I tried to optimize too early?

messages.subject: Re: reactive expression didn't update when reactive source changed(item in list)
parts:
In my previous reply I was trying to introduce as less things as possible from a complex framework, then I forgot one important point:

Page C is to detect outliers in data and remove some points, so it need to update the whole data set...

At first I tried to create a reactive value of points to be removed, then let page A to update plots based on this reactive expression. Later I found I need to update at least subset data in page C, because there could be multiple iterations of 
1. remove some points, 
2. make some calculations again 
3. try to find if there is still points to remove 

Each iteration need to update data so the calculation can be based on updated data. I decided to put all the update code in the observer of "remove points", and that will change the whole data. (I saved the removed points so the changes can be undo)

So this is why I need to change the whole data instead of a subset or a copy. It has been some time since I worked on this page, and today I need to fix a new discovered bug, so I was right in choosing update whole data, but forgot the complete reason of this.

One solution I tried today is update whole data when user switched to page C. Make sure it trigger changes in select_data by assign NULL first to the data.table object. The disadvantage of this is that switching to C then A will cause the plot refresh.

So I moved back to my original approach, which actually did the extra calculations needed by page C in page A. I found pure math calculation is often faster than plot refreshes.

The reason that I want to try different approach today is that I found some data break the extra column calculation in page C, and I wanted to isolate that to page C only, so I asked the original question and tried various methods. Now I just will add some more robust method to make sure it doesn't fail with new data.

parts:
OK. For things like "remove some points" (and especially if it needs to happen multiple times) then there will definitely need to be some (reactive) state kept somewhere and updated. However, this does NOT mean that these other processes that augment the data frame with additional columns should also be modifying that state. They can still be modeled as reactive expressions that augment the (now-stateful) data.

For representing the data with user-selected points excluded, you can go one of two ways: either have a data frame/table that you remove rows from and then overwrite (as you are doing today), or, leave the original data frame/table alone, and keep a separate vector of row numbers that should be removed. This latter approach can benefit if the removal of rows doesn't inherently necessitate the recalculation of the extra columns; you only have to do the extra-column calculations once, over the whole data, and remove the rows from the already-enhanced table.

I hope this still is still making sense to you, it's hard to do this without working off of an actual concrete example.

On Wednesday, May 10, 2017 at 2:46:12 PM UTC-4, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
It's true that modifying a data.table won't trigger reactivity. We don't have any way to know the data table object has changed.

Also, modifying a reactive values object is an example of a side effect and therefore should be done in an observer, not a reactive expression. If you don't know what I'm talking about, the "Effective reactive programming" videos on https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/ go into side effects and observers/reactives in some detail.
